clue.text: Elegiac notes not caught by late writer

blocks.note: first meaning: the bugle call sounded at military funerals and remembrance services
second meaning: the final mail collection of the day, which a tardy letter-writer misses

explanation.surface: A belated poet fails to catch a sorrowful melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late writer' suggests a dead author; read literally it is someone writing a letter too late in the day to make the final collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call played at military funerals is mournful music, and the day's final mail collection is what a tardy correspondent misses.

clue.text: Record spread of snarl-up

blocks.note: a record is a log
jam is a spread for bread

explanation.surface: Recording how a traffic tangle is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about the snarl-up; it is a noun, something spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl-up is a blockage or deadlock, and the answer names a blockage like logs choking a river.

clue.text: Heathen is sensible to accept a Bible

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a sensible person is sage, wise
taken as written
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible; with the A above it makes that abbreviation

explanation.surface: A heathen is wise enough to take up the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorized (King James) Version, is the standard abbreviation for the Bible; 'a Bible' supplies both letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathen was once used, pejoratively, of an uncivilised or barbarous person, which is the noun sense here.

clue.text: Around arrival of rain, petal was knocked about

indicators.note: something knocked about is battered out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: When the rain came, a flower petal got buffeted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around arrival' looks like part of the weather scene; it is the definition, meaning the time around a baby's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term describes the period immediately before and after birth, when a baby arrives.

clue.text: Not much work for judge, deprived of power by this?

blocks.note: not much is short
judges travel a circuit, a round of courts in a region

explanation.surface: A judge with little work loses power because of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A circuit is the regional round of courts a British judge travels; the question mark flags the electrical sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty electrical connection that bypasses the load blows fuses and cuts off supply, leaving a house without electricity.

clue.text: Put out for audience, not all at once

indicators.note: something done for an audience is heard rather than read, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: put out means disconcerted or flustered

explanation.surface: Something is staged for spectators gradually rather than in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'staged' beside 'audience'; it means flustered, and that word is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A change introduced in stages over time, rather than in a single step, is described as being done gradually in successive steps.

clue.text: Why dragon may guard something hard to destroy

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so the letters are held inside the words

blocks.note: inside wHY DRAgon

explanation.surface: Wondering why a dragon would protect a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hydra was the many-headed monster of Greek myth that grew two heads for each one cut off; it fits the dragon picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical beast grew new heads when one was severed, so the name is used for any evil that keeps returning.

clue.text: Insist on buying Irishman a drink?

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to buy it for them
Pat is the stock Irish name in crosswords
surface padding that tells you which sense of buying is meant

explanation.surface: Someone insists on treating an Irish friend to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drink?' tells you which sense of buying: to stand someone a round. The phrase comes from poker, refusing to draw new cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The poker idiom means to hold firm and refuse to change one's position, which is to insist on it.

clue.text: No confidence in group of companies headed by girls

indicators.note: a thing headed by something has that something placed at its front, fixing the order of the parts

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, so two girls are Dis
a trust is a combine of businesses

explanation.surface: Doubts about a corporate group run by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headed by' means the girls go in front; Di (short for Diana) is a stock crossword girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no confidence in someone means lacking faith in them, which is suspicion or doubt.

clue.text: Pontius Pilate, or his dad?

blocks.note: first meaning: Pilate was the Roman official ruling Judaea
second meaning: old British slang for one's father or boss

explanation.surface: A question of whether Pilate or his father is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The governor' (or 'the guv'nor') is informal British slang for one's father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilate held the post of Roman prefect administering Judaea, and British slang calls a father or boss by this title.

clue.text: One has business with models

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
business transactions are deals

explanation.surface: Someone does business alongside fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' suggests catwalk people; here it means perfect examples to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Models in the sense of perfect examples worth imitating are standards of perfection one aims for.

clue.text: Bismarck was originally really rather poor

blocks.note: 'honest!' is said to mean 'really!'
the comparative of broke, so poorer than average

explanation.surface: The German statesman started out quite poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' suggests a first letter; it simply means Bismarck first coined this title for himself at the 1878 Congress of Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismarck famously described his role as an impartial mediator between the powers using this phrase.

clue.text: Special vocabulary lacking its principal element

indicators.note: without its principal, the leading letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the specialised language of a trade

explanation.surface: A specialist vocabulary missing its key component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal element' reads as one phrase; split it so 'principal' means the first letter and 'element' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a noble gas, number 18 in the periodic table, so it is a chemical element.

clue.text: Play — not The Third Man

blocks.note: surface reading: a drama, but not the famous Graham Greene film
setter's reading: a stage play with no third actor, only a cast of a pair

explanation.surface: Recommending a drama other than the classic film noir.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man is a 1949 film; read literally, a play without a third man has only two performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage piece written for just two actors is a play from which any third performer is absent.

clue.text: It ornaments the church, disgraces the pub

blocks.note: first meaning: coloured window panes decorating churches
second meaning: a dirty, smeared drinking vessel is a poor show in a bar

explanation.surface: Something adorns a church but shames a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is decoration in a church window and a grubby tumbler on a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured window panes decorate churches, while a smeared, dirty tumbler served in a bar reflects badly on the landlord.

clue.text: Charity has efficient factory

blocks.note: first meaning: charitable deeds
second meaning: a works is a factory, and a well-run one is good

explanation.surface: A charity owns a well-run plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable deeds done for others are virtuous acts, and a works is a British term for a factory or plant.

clue.text: Abandoned bra in bed, and left bloomers here?

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Underwear abandoned in bed, with knickers left about too.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers look like underwear beside the bra, but a bloomer is a British crusty loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a large crusty loaf, so a kitchen container for loaves is where such things would be kept.

clue.text: On which Al types can speak?

definitions.text: On which Al types can speak?

blocks.note: surface reading: people like Al Capone, gangsters talking

blocks.clueFragment: On which Al types can speak?
blocks.note: setter's reading: motorists on the A1, Britain's Great North Road, making calls while driving

explanation.surface: A device that lets gangland types like Al talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, and the printed letters also nod to Al Capone, whose surname echoes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile telephone fitted in a vehicle lets motorists hold conversations while driving.

clue.text: Transfer from existing place

blocks.note: something existing is real
a place is a location

explanation.surface: Moving something from where it currently sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer, as a noun, is the act of moving resources or people to a different use or post.

clue.text: Little cover to be found in small island

blocks.note: first meaning: a skimpy two-piece swimsuit
second meaning: the Pacific atoll the swimsuit is named after

explanation.surface: Scant shelter available on a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimsuit took its name from the Marshall Islands atoll used for 1946 nuclear tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief two-piece swimsuit covers very little, and a Pacific atoll in the Marshall Islands shares the name.

clue.text: Student, last to practise, fit for concert

indicators.note: the last of the word means only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British student driver's car
the final letter of practise
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: A music student is finally fit to play in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' suggests music; here it means agreement or alliance, as in acting in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together in alliance, and an alliance of parties is a confederation or union.

clue.text: Does it explain more about hi-fi equipment?

blocks.note: first meaning: one who amplifies a statement expands on it
second meaning: the unit in a stereo system that boosts the signal

explanation.surface: Asking whether a manual says more about stereo gear.
explanation.walkthrough: To amplify a remark is to add detail to it, so one who does that explains more.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereo unit boosting signal strength shares its name with someone who expands on a statement with further detail.

clue.text: Sally may be my daughter

blocks.note: first meaning: a sortie, a going out
second meaning: a child is one's offspring

explanation.surface: A parent says Sally might be their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a girl's name; lowercase it is a sudden outward rush, and a child is a parent's offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally is to go forth suddenly, as troops pour out; and a person's children are their legal offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Colourless counter-revolutionary

blocks.note: first meaning: pale, without colour
second meaning: the anti-Bolshevik side in the Russian Civil War

explanation.walkthrough: In the Russian Civil War the Reds were the revolutionaries and their opponents were known by this colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and lacking hue is one sense; the other names the anti-Bolshevik forces fighting the Reds after 1917.

clue.text: Very fat — made two holes in colourful jacket

definitions.text: made two holes in colourful jacket

blocks.note: first meaning: bloated, gross and ruddy-faced

blocks.clueFragment: made two holes in colourful jacket
blocks.note: second part: unresolved; the setter's exact mechanism here is not established

explanation.surface: Someone hugely overweight burst two holes in a gaudy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCERTAIN: the crossings and 'Very fat' fix the answer, but how the second half yields it is unclear; treat that half's reading as unconfirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a coarse, bloated, red-faced person, so it covers someone grossly overweight and florid.

clue.text: Avoiding the border along the bottom of the wall

definitions.text: the border along the bottom of the wall

blocks.note: first meaning: going round something rather than facing it

blocks.clueFragment: the border along the bottom of the wall
blocks.note: second meaning: the board fixed where a wall meets the floor

explanation.surface: Someone steering clear of the edge at the foot of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is short for skirting board, the British name for a baseboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Going around an issue instead of tackling it, and the British term for the baseboard running round a room's walls.

clue.text: Went without being massaged, I hear

indicators.note: the speaker says this is what they heard, so the sound of a word matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: massaged muscles are worked with the hands like dough

explanation.surface: Someone left without getting their massage, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the massage word is pronounced exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without something is to lack it, and lacking something means you required it.

clue.text: Ancient spirit disturbed by extremes of noise

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, the first and the last
disturbed things are thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of noise

explanation.surface: An old ghost is unsettled by the edges of a din.
explanation.walkthrough: The modern sense is 'unspoilt'; the older sense, from Latin pristinus, is 'original, of former times'.
explanation.definitionFit: In its original sense the word means belonging to the earliest period, primitive or of former times.
